title: SLO health scoring and smart pager routing for burn-rate & anomalies
creator: Aisha Carter
description: Problem: Our current SLO alerting is brittle and noisy during platform-wide transient spikes. Burn-rate alerts trigger paging too often, and teams lack a unified signal that combines latency trends, error budget consumption, and anomalous behaviour detected in traces/logs. Goal: implement a composite 'SLO health score' and a smart-pager routing policy that reduces noisy pages while ensuring high-severity degradations are paged immediately. Scope: 1) Add tracing hooks to emit latency and error features per-route/route-group to metrics pipeline. 2) Enrich metrics/log pipeline with a burn-rate recording rule, sliding-window error budget calculator, and an anomaly_score time series. 3) Build a new SLO Health dashboard and recording rule for 'slo_health_score' used by Alertmanager rules to decide page vs ticket. 4) Implement smart-pager receiver and escalation policy in Alertmanager/opsgenie integration.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A single prometheus-style recording rule 'slo_health_score' exists and is computed from 50th/95th latency percentiles, error_budget_remaining_pct, and anomaly_score. 2) Burn-rate alerts fire as events to the alert pipeline but only escalate to paging if slo_health_score < 40 for 3m and burn_rate > 3x baseline. 3) On-call routing respects service ownership tags and uses staggered escalation windows (team -> product oncall -> platform SRE). 4) Dashboards show slice-by-route breakdown and top contributing traces/logs for any triggered SLO event. 5) We have a rollback plan and playbook documented for false positives.
technical_design: Tracing hooks: add an outbound span hook in the runtime router that attaches 'route_id', 'model_variant', and an observed 'server_latency_ms' tag to root spans; ensure these are ingested by the tracing collector and turned into metrics via metric-extraction rules. Metrics pipeline: add a new Vector/Prometheus recording pipeline to compute sliding-window quantiles (p50/p95), request counts, error counts, and error_budget_consumption_rate. Burn-rate: implement a 5m/1h dual-window burn-rate calculation with recording rules to power short-term and medium-term burn detection. Anomaly detection: implement an online EWMA-based anomaly_score operator in the metrics aggregator that produces a 0-100 anomaly_score; this operator includes seasonality dampening and outlier trimming to avoid transient spikes. SLO Health Score: composite formula (normalized latency_score + error_budget_remaining_weighted + inverse_anomaly_score) producing 0-100. Alerting: update Alertmanager with two paths: INCIDENT (pager) and OBSERVABILITY-TICKET (no immediate page). Use template variables to include top-5 trace IDs and log links in the alert payload. Smart pager routing: use ownership label 'svc_owner_team' from service catalog to resolve routing and to apply escalation delays.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable metrics extraction and slo_health_score for three non-critical services (auth-staging, embedding-worker-staging, routing-test) for 2 weeks and monitor. Phase 2 (opt-in): expose slo_health_score as opt-in for customer-facing services behind feature flag for 1 month. Phase 3 (platform): enable default for all services with standard escalation policy; monitor false-positive rate and adjust anomaly thresholds. Rollback: revert recording rules and switch Alertmanager receiver to legacy paging. Communication: notify oncall@redwood, weekly #observability sync, and post runbook to Confluence.
